description:
Found s361 probing perl's t/comp/uproto.t (the #153 step-3b arity work). Pre-existing.

  sub mymkdir (_;$) { print "@_\n" }
  $_ = "mydir";
  mymkdir();            # perl: "mydir"    PCL: "" (empty @_)

perl's `_` prototype slot means "this argument defaults to $_ when the call
supplies none" — the whole point of the character.  PCL parses `_` into a
param (the s361 arity work relies on that: it counts toward max-args, and
`mymkdir foo => 0755` now correctly passes BOTH args), but the DEFAULT is
never materialised, so a no-arg call passes an empty list.

Note the sibling that already works and should be the model: the builtin
named-unary family defaults to `$_` via Config.pm's `[1,-2]` spec
(`known_no_of_params`), i.e. PCL already has one mechanism for "defaults to
$_".  Per CLAUDE.md 11 the fix should route the `_` prototype slot into that
same mechanism rather than adding a second one.

Scope note: only the ZERO-arg call is wrong; `f($x)` and `f $x, $y` are
correct as of s361 (1279be6).</description>
</invoke>


s429 (Fable) matrix row, perl vs PCL, while shipping #259: `sub f (_) { "f(" . join(",", map { defined $_ ? $_ : "u" } @_) . ")" }  print "R=", (f || 5), "\n";`
  perl: R=f(u)   (the `_` default supplies $_ at the call site; $_ undef here)
  PCL:  R=f()    (no argument)
After #259 `(_)` classifies as a named unary (spec 1) â the PARSE is right; only the
call-site `$_` default is missing.  Config's convention has a slot for it (-2 = "defaults
to $_"), and add_implicit_default_param acts on -2 â but it reads known_no_of_params
directly; routing it through no_params_of_sub (so a user `(_)` answers -2 there too) is
the reuse-don't-duplicate shape.  Probe `f;` at end of expression and `f || 5` both.
subject: The `_` prototype does not default to $_ — `sub f (_) {…}; f();` passes nothing
